intervals.note: REWRITTEN 2026-10-25 (before: start 2018, approximate, from a PRD acceptance month; end open). HAYSTAC's own 2026 paper dates data-taking: phase I January 2016 to July 2017; phase II in sub-phases (II(a) September 2019-April 2020, II(b) July 2021-November 2021, II(c)/(d) September 2022-August 2024, II(e) July 2022); no data-taking is dated after August 2024, and an APS abstract of 19 March 2026 says the experiment is upgrading for Phase III (next row). The sub-phase gaps between runs are not separate intervals.

intervals.label: Phase III upgrade (multi-rod cavity) and commissioning at Yale
intervals.note: APS Global Physics Summit abstract, 19 March 2026: "In preparation for Phase III, HAYSTAC is currently upgrading to a multi-rod cavity ... summarize the Phase III testing and commissioning at Yale" (7-rod cavity, 5.5-7.3 GHz); a second abstract says the new high-resolution channel "will be commissioned for HAYSTAC Phase III". Phase II data-taking ended in August 2024 (arXiv:2510.15848v3). No source dated after March 2026 says whether Phase III data-taking has started, so the upgrade is kept open at 2026-10-25; a conference listing for November 2026 whose text a search showed ("for Phase III, HAYSTAC upgraded to a multi-rod cavity") could not be opened, and is not used.
intervals.quote: In preparation for Phase III, HAYSTAC is currently upgrading to a multi-rod cavity that can perform high-frequency searches with a high FOM

placements.quote: The detector was built and is in operation at Yale University's Wright laboratory.

summary.plain: The HAYSTAC detector uses a strong magnet and a tunable metal cavity, plus quantum-noise-reducing electronics, to search for faint signals from dark-matter axions converting into radio photons.
summary.technical: Tunable microwave cavity haloscope at Yale Wright Laboratory using inverse-Primakoff axion-to-photon conversion in a static magnetic field, with a Josephson parametric amplifier / squeezed-vacuum receiver for sub-quantum-limited noise.

technology.value: Microwave-cavity haloscope using a strong static magnetic field (inverse Primakoff conversion) with quantum-electronics/cavity-QED readout, including a squeezed-vacuum receiver to beat the standard quantum noise limit.
